sentences.text: This animal possessed distinctively thick osteoderms, the bony plates in its skin, which lacked the pitting found in most other crocodilians.
The most common fossil remains are its unusual blunt, conical teeth adapted for crushing hard food items.
These teeth featured a wrinkled enamel surface with prominent annual growth rings and vertical ridges.
The type species B. harlani had a short, massive lower jaw that was nearly circular in cross-section.
A juvenile jaw found at the boundary likely represents a mass death event following the extinction.
The genus Bottosaurus was first described by Louis Agassiz in 1849.
Phylogenetic studies from the 2010s classify Bottosaurus within the subfamily Caimaninae, making it more closely related to modern caimans than to alligators.
The Spanish Wikipedia entry classifies Bottosaurus within the family Crocodylidae.
Fossils of Bottosaurus date from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous to the Paleocene epoch.
Bottosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous and Early Paleocene in New Jersey, Texas, and possibly North Carolina and South Carolina.
The species Bottosaurus fustidens was described from the middle Paleocene of western Texas.
Bottosaurus is predominantly found in Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian strata, including the Hornerstown Formation, New Jersey Greensands, and Laramie Formation.
The time range for Bottosaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 56 million years ago.
